item.title: Paired DNA strands recognize shape, not just sequence, in new small-molecule sensing method
item.description: You have probably performed a sandwich assay before, even if you didn't know it. After a sample is dripped onto the test strip, it combines with detector antibodies attached to tiny gold particles, which bind to any viral proteins present. When the sample reaches the test line, a second antibody anchored to the strip binds to a different site on the viral protein, creating a molecular "sandwich." item.description: Around 450 million metric tons of plastics are produced worldwide each year. item.title: New tests expand empathy measurement to joyful stories and embarrassing mishaps
item.description: Listening to someone recount their visit to an amusement park can feel like being on an emotional roller coaster yourself. Even if the listeners have never set foot in the park, they can still empathize with the other person's feelings: the deep disappointment when it turns out that their favorite ride is closed. The joy—at having the best ice cream of their life. And the embarrassment—after that ice cream abruptly left their stomach on the Freefall Tower. Put simply: whatever the other person is feeling, we feel it with them. Fuente: Phys.org.

Detrás de este movimiento encontramos una preocupación que va más allá de una mala jornada bursátil: el temor a que la expansión de la inteligencia artificial encuentre obstáculos y no consiga mantener el ritmo de crecimiento… Fuente: Xataka.
